subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion contract now, and should it apply to builtin indexing only or also to QMD, watcher behavior, status diagnostics, and index identity?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes which files enter recall context, while repository policy treats config/default and memory/session-state surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Land the open excludePaths candidate or successor after fixing merge semantics and index identity, with explicit docs that QMD parity remains separately tracked.

options.title: Require cross-backend parity
options.body: Pause the candidate until builtin, QMD, watcher behavior, docs, and status diagnostics share one exclusion/path-hygiene model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and improve guidance/warnings around path drift, broad extraPaths, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Land the open excludePaths candidate or successor after fixing merge semantics and index identity, with explicit docs that QMD parity remains separately tracked.

likelyOwner.reason: The current memory-host and manager-state history makes this the best available owner for the config/runtime boundary decision.
